messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: dplyr impact on row names
parts:
Hi All,

I've been fiddling around with dplyr & row names. Since it messes with them I figured a good approach was to manage id information in variables and then put them into the row.names position only right before you need them for a function that reports its values. When I did that and printed, it looked like they were over-written again. But that's not the case. tbl_df() doesn't over-write them, print.tbl_df() just hides them from you, giving you the impression that they've been over-written. See example below.

Cheers,
Bob

> # Create some data
> id <- 1:200 * 10
> gender <- rep(c("m","f"), 100)
> y  <- rnorm(200)
> 
> # Put vars in a data frame, with id in row.names
> mydata <- data.frame(id, gender, y)
> row.names(mydata) <- id
> head(mydata)
   id gender         y
10 10      m -0.039229
20 20      f -0.304203
30 30      m  0.134969
40 40      f -1.496139
50 50      m  0.913439
60 60      f  0.497791
> 
> # Convert it to a tbl_df and examine row names
> mytable <- tbl_df(mydata)
> print(mytable)
Source: local data frame [200 x 3]

    id gender         y
1   10      m -0.039229
2   20      f -0.304203
3   30      m  0.134969
4   40      f -1.496139
5   50      m  0.913439
6   60      f  0.497791
7   70      m  0.606355
8   80      f -0.569477
9   90      m -0.524492
10 100      f -3.311762
.. ...    ...       ...
> head(mytable)
Source: local data frame [6 x 3]

  id gender         y
1 10      m -0.039229
2 20      f -0.304203
3 30      m  0.134969
4 40      f -1.496139
5 50      m  0.913439
6 60      f  0.497791
> 
> # Question: did tbl_df() destroy the row names,
> # or is print() overwriting them temporarily?
> 
> # They're still there
> head(as.data.frame(mytable))
   id gender         y
10 10      m -0.039229
20 20      f -0.304203
30 30      m  0.134969
40 40      f -1.496139
50 50      m  0.913439
60 60      f  0.497791

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: dplyr impact on row names
parts:
Yes, I don't remove them so you can later use add_rownames() (new in
dplyr 0.4) to convert them back to proper variables.

Hadley
